paragraphs: 4Diffusion turns a video from a single viewpoint into a representation of a three-dimensional scene that changes over time. The challenge is keeping appearance consistent across both viewpoints and moments. Existing approaches can produce flicker and temporal inconsistencies when they lack joint spatial and temporal modeling or combine guidance from several diffusion models.

The authors build a unified model for generating videos from multiple views. They add a trainable motion module to a frozen diffusion model that already understands three-dimensional structure. Training on a curated dataset gives the combined model reasonable temporal consistency while preserving the original model's spatial consistency and generalization capabilities.

This model then guides optimization of a dynamic neural radiance field through a proposed 4D-aware score distillation loss. An additional anchor loss improves appearance details and helps the representation learn. Qualitative and quantitative experiments report better performance than previous methods. The central contribution is coordinated guidance across space and time, aimed at reducing the disagreements that arise when separate diffusion models guide the same reconstruction.
neurips-2024-4diffusion-multi-view-video.tldr: 4Diffusion uses unified multi-view video diffusion guidance to generate more spatially and temporally consistent 4D content from a monocular video.

paragraphs: This paper argues that evaluating a language model requires looking beyond how often its answers are correct. Uncertainty provides another dimension: a model's accuracy and its degree of certainty need not move together. The authors introduce an evaluation approach that incorporates uncertainty quantification into comparisons of large language models.

Their examination covers nine language models or model series across five representative natural language processing tasks. The results reveal several departures from a simple expectation that stronger models should also be more certain. Higher accuracy can accompany lower certainty, and larger models can show greater uncertainty than smaller counterparts. Instruction fine-tuning also tends to increase uncertainty in their evaluation.

These are qualified empirical findings, rather than universal rules about model size or training. Their significance is that an accuracy ranking alone can conceal differences in how models express uncertainty. By measuring both dimensions, the proposed benchmark gives a broader picture of model behavior and makes those differences part of the evaluation rather than leaving them unexamined.
neurips-2024-benchmarking-llms-via-uncer.tldr: An uncertainty-aware benchmark shows that greater language-model accuracy or size does not necessarily come with greater certainty.

paragraphs: BLAST addresses the computational burden of the dense matrix operations used throughout large neural networks. These operations are central to linear layers, so representing their weights more efficiently can reduce inference complexity. The paper introduces a structured matrix representation that adapts at the block level to capture useful patterns in those weights.

Its distinguishing feature is flexibility. BLAST can represent several kinds of structure, either learned during training or obtained from existing weight matrices. This lets the authors study both training models with structured weights and compressing larger pretrained models, using the same general representation across language and vision tasks.

For the medium-sized ViT and GPT-2 models, training with BLAST improves performance while reducing complexity by 70% and 40%, respectively. For Llama-7B and DiT-XL, it achieves twofold compression with the smallest performance loss among the structured matrices tested. These results support the value of adaptable structure: in the reported comparisons, efficiency gains need not require the same performance tradeoff as more restrictive structured representations.
neurips-2024-blast-block-level-adaptive-.tldr: BLAST compresses neural-network weights with flexible block-level structure, reducing complexity while preserving or improving performance in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: ChatQA is a collection of models and training methods for conversational question answering and retrieval-augmented generation, where retrieved information supports an answer. The paper tackles both generation and retrieval. A two-stage instruction-tuning procedure improves generation, while a dense retriever is optimized specifically for questions arising in conversation.

The retriever produces results comparable to leading query-rewriting alternatives while substantially reducing deployment costs. To evaluate the overall approach, the authors introduce ChatRAG Bench: ten datasets covering retrieval-supported answers, questions about tables, arithmetic, and questions that cannot be answered from the available information. This makes the comparison broader than a single question-answering task.

On this benchmark, the Llama2-based ChatQA-1.0-70B scores 54.14, slightly above the two cited GPT-4 versions at 53.90 and 54.03, without synthetic training data from OpenAI GPT models. The Llama3-based version also surpasses the cited GPT-4-Turbo model. These benchmark-specific results support the proposed training recipe. The authors release model weights, tuning data, the benchmark, and the retriever to support further research.
neurips-2024-chatqa-surpassing-gpt-4-on-.tldr: ChatQA combines conversational retrieval and two-stage instruction tuning to outperform the cited GPT-4 models on ChatRAG Bench.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to choose useful image-text examples from noisy datasets for training vision-language models. Its focus is improving the selection metric applied to CLIP embeddings, rather than requiring a specialized new embedding model. Better selection can make the same pool of candidate training data more useful for downstream tasks.

The first method, negCLIPLoss, extends a score based only on an image and its paired text. It also accounts for alignment with contrastive pairs, using those comparisons as an additional normalization term. The second method, NormSim, applies when the downstream task is known and measures similarity between candidate pretraining data and the target data.

On DataComp, the methods improve ImageNet-1k performance by 5.3% and performance across 38 downstream tasks by 2.8% relative to the best baseline using only OpenAI's CLIP-L/14. They also work alongside existing selection techniques. Combining them with DFN and HYPE improves average downstream performance by 0.9%, establishing the reported state of the art on DataComp-medium. The results show that selection rules themselves offer gains beyond changing the model that supplies embeddings.
neurips-2024-cliploss-and-norm-based-dat.tldr: negCLIPLoss and NormSim improve image-text data selection by considering contrastive comparisons and, when available, similarity to target-task data.

paragraphs: CORY explores a cooperative alternative to conventional reinforcement-learning fine-tuning of language models. The motivation is that PPO and related methods can perform poorly or suffer distribution collapse in this setting. The authors turn fine-tuning into a sequential interaction between two agents created by duplicating the language model.

One agent acts as a pioneer, producing an answer directly from the query. The other acts as an observer, receiving both the query and the pioneer's response before producing its own answer. Both agents train together and periodically swap roles. This arrangement lets each agent experience generating an initial response and responding with another agent's output as additional context.

The experiments fine-tune GPT-2 and Llama-2 on IMDB Review and GSM8K using subjective and objective reward functions, respectively. CORY outperforms PPO in the reported evaluations of policy optimality, resistance to distribution collapse, and training robustness. These findings support sequential cooperation as a promising training mechanism for the tested settings, with broader application presented as potential rather than an established universal advantage.
neurips-2024-coevolving-with-the-other-y.tldr: CORY fine-tunes two cooperating copies of a language model and outperforms PPO on the reported training-quality and robustness evaluations.

paragraphs: Standard analyses of gradient descent often describe an objective using a global worst-case measure of how quickly its gradient can change. Such a measure may poorly reflect the regions that optimization actually visits. This paper develops bounds on remaining optimization error that instead depend on the conditioning encountered along the optimization path.

The key quantity is directional smoothness, which measures gradient variation in a relevant direction. The authors use it to construct upper bounds on the objective. Minimizing those bounds produces implicit equations for strongly adapted step sizes. For convex quadratic objectives, these equations are straightforward to solve and provide new guarantees for two classical step-size choices.

The analysis also covers the Polyak step size and normalized gradient descent for general functions, proving fast path-dependent rates without requiring knowledge of directional smoothness. Logistic-regression experiments show tighter convergence guarantees than classical smoothness-based theory. The contribution is therefore both explanatory and analytical: familiar optimization methods can receive guarantees that better reflect the geometry they actually encounter during a run.
neurips-2024-directional-smoothness-and-.tldr: Directional smoothness yields gradient-descent guarantees that reflect the optimization path rather than global worst-case behavior.

paragraphs: Entity alignment identifies entries in two knowledge graphs that refer to the same entity, enabling the graphs to be merged. Human labels can be costly because annotation may require expertise across domains. LLM4EA investigates using language models to supply annotations while addressing two obstacles: the large space of possible matches and errors in generated labels.

The framework uses an active-learning policy to prioritize valuable entities for annotation. That policy considers relationships both within each graph and across the two graphs, reducing the annotation space. An unsupervised label-refinement component then uses probabilistic reasoning to improve label accuracy, rather than treating every language-model annotation as reliable.

The process is iterative: feedback from an underlying entity-alignment model helps improve the selection policy. Experiments on four benchmark datasets report advantages in effectiveness, robustness, and efficiency. The approach matters because it treats annotation selection and annotation quality as connected problems. Language-model semantic knowledge becomes part of a feedback-driven alignment system that explicitly accounts for noisy labels.
neurips-2024-entity-alignment-with-noisy.tldr: LLM4EA combines selective language-model annotation, probabilistic label refinement, and alignment-model feedback to match entities across knowledge graphs.

paragraphs: G2D addresses a mismatch between common medical image pretraining and tasks that require precise localization. Aligning a whole image with a whole radiology report can teach clinically relevant information, but it gives less support to learning detailed pixel-level features. Those localized features matter when pathological patterns are subtle or confined to small regions.

The framework learns whole-image and dense visual representations together using image-text pairs without additional annotations. Its central addition is a pseudo-segmentation task that encourages learning local visual information during pretraining. The masks for that task are generated during training, and their generation introduces no extra trainable parameters.

The authors report superior performance across five medical imaging tasks and 25 diseases. In segmentation, G2D surpasses existing models while using only 1% of the fine-tuning data, compared with 100% for the other models. This result supports the idea that teaching localization during pretraining can make later segmentation learning substantially more data-efficient in the evaluated setting.
neurips-2024-g2d-from-global-to-dense-ra.tldr: G2D adds pseudo-segmentation to medical image-text pretraining, improving localized representations and reported segmentation data efficiency.

paragraphs: This paper investigates how diffusion models learn to combine features in new ways. Rather than studying the full complexity of natural images, the authors conduct controlled experiments with conditional diffusion models generating forms of two-dimensional Gaussian data. This reduced setting lets them examine the organization of learned representations and its relationship to compositional behavior.

The models learn partially continuous, factorized representations. Independent underlying variations occupy orthogonal directions, but representations for different values of the same feature do not align. This distinction explains the observed combination of strong compositionality and limited interpolation: recombining features and generating unseen values within a feature are different capabilities.

The experiments also show that a small amount of compositional training examples can be enough for the models to acquire compositionality. The authors connect the formation of representation manifolds to percolation theory, offering an account of its sudden emergence. These findings provide insight from a deliberately simplified setting and suggest directions for training diffusion models, while extensions to real-world generation remain a motivation for future research.
neurips-2024-how-diffusion-models-learn-.tldr: Controlled Gaussian-data experiments reveal how diffusion models can learn compositional representations while still struggling to interpolate unseen feature values.

paragraphs: The authors propose a hypothesis about how multilingual processing is distributed across a language model's layers. In their MWork account, early layers interpret multilingual input and convert it into English for task solving. Intermediate layers use English for processing while incorporating multilingual knowledge, and final layers produce an answer in the query's original language.

To investigate this account, they introduce Parallel Language-specific Neuron Detection, which finds neurons activated by different languages without labeled data. They then deactivate language-specific neurons in different layers and network structures. These intervention experiments support the proposed workflow, including distinct roles for self-attention and feed-forward structures in intermediate processing.

The account also motivates a targeted fine-tuning method that updates language-specific neurons using a small dataset. In the reported experiments, it improves the selected language without compromising others. With 400 documents, average gains are 3.6% for high-resource languages and 2.3% for low-resource languages across tasks. The contribution connects an experimentally supported processing hypothesis to a practical way of improving multilingual capabilities.
neurips-2024-how-do-large-language-model.tldr: Neuron-intervention experiments support a proposed multilingual processing workflow and motivate targeted fine-tuning that improves language-specific performance.

paragraphs: A neural network update can change predictions for states that were absent from the training batch. This paper calls those uncontrolled changes churn and studies their consequences in reinforcement learning. The concern is especially relevant because value estimates and policies influence each other throughout training, so a change can propagate beyond its immediate source.

The authors analyze churn through generalized policy iteration with function approximation. They identify a chain effect in which changes to value estimation and policy improvement compound and bias subsequent learning. They examine concrete manifestations: altered greedy actions in value-based methods, trust-region violations in proximal policy optimization, and coupled policy-value bias in actor-critic methods.

Their proposed method, CHAIN, reduces this chain effect and can be incorporated into most existing deep reinforcement-learning algorithms. Experiments show reduced churn and improved learning across online and offline settings, including both value-based and policy-based approaches. The findings make uncontrolled changes outside an update batch a concrete target for improving training, rather than treating each update's effects as confined to the states it directly uses.
neurips-2024-improving-deep-reinforcemen.tldr: CHAIN improves reinforcement learning by reducing compounding unintended changes between value estimates and policies.

paragraphs: Training Gaussian-process hyperparameters on very large datasets can require expensive repeated linear-system solves. Iterative approaches use solvers such as conjugate gradients, alternating projections, or stochastic gradient descent to estimate the marginal-likelihood gradient. This paper proposes three improvements that apply across these solvers and make better use of computation during hyperparameter optimization.

First, a pathwise gradient estimator reduces the number of solver iterations needed and spreads out the computational cost of prediction. Second, warm starting uses the previous optimization step's solution as the next solver's starting point. This accelerates convergence with a reported negligible bias. Third, early stopping limits the computation spent on each solve.

Warm starting and early stopping reinforce each other: progress from a partially completed solve can carry into later marginal-likelihood steps. The reported techniques deliver speedups of up to 72 times when solving to a specified tolerance and reduce average residual norm by up to seven times when stopping early. These are maximum reported gains, demonstrating the potential value of carrying solver progress across optimization steps.
neurips-2024-improving-linear-system-sol.tldr: A pathwise estimator, warm starts, and early stopping accelerate iterative Gaussian-process hyperparameter optimization by reusing computational progress.

paragraphs: Self-training uses a model's own predictions as labels for further learning. Under a distribution shift, confidence can become less closely related to accuracy, making those pseudo-labels unreliable. This paper develops a temporal approach to improving them, motivated by the observation that information from learning over time can help regulate later training.

The method constructs an uncertainty-aware temporal ensemble with a simple relative threshold. It uses that ensemble to smooth noisy pseudo-labels and encourage consistency selectively across time. The central idea is to incorporate the history and uncertainty of predictions into label correction, rather than relying only on the current prediction's confidence.

The authors prove that their temporal ensemble is asymptotically correct and that the smoothing technique can reduce self-training's optimality gap. Asymptotic correctness concerns eventual behavior, while the gap reduction is stated as a possibility supported by their analysis. Experiments report improvements of 8% to 16% across diverse distribution shifts without computational overhead, alongside better calibration and robustness to hyperparameter choices. Together, the findings support temporal consistency as an efficient correction mechanism.
neurips-2024-improving-self-training-und.tldr: An uncertainty-aware temporal ensemble improves pseudo-labels under distribution shifts, with theoretical support and reported self-training gains of 8% to 16%.

paragraphs: An externality occurs when an action affects someone else without compensation. Many economic treatments assume participants already know the environment and their preferences, which makes their conclusions harder to apply when people must learn through interaction. This paper studies that uncertainty in a two-player bandit game where one player's actions affect the other.

The authors revisit the Coase theorem's connection between property rights, bargaining, transfers, and total welfare. In their online setting, they first show that welfare breaks down when property rights are absent. This establishes a problem within the specified learning game, rather than presuming that individually chosen actions will automatically produce a good combined outcome.

They then provide a policy through which the players learn a bargaining strategy that maximizes total welfare. The result recovers a Coase-style conclusion under uncertainty in the considered setting. Its significance is that the welfare benefit of bargaining need not depend on participants possessing perfect knowledge from the outset: an appropriate learning policy can support that outcome as interaction proceeds.
neurips-2024-learning-to-mitigate-extern.tldr: In a two-player bandit game, a learned bargaining policy recovers a Coase-style welfare-maximizing outcome without perfect initial knowledge.

paragraphs: Hyperparameter optimization has two interacting levels: an inner process trains the model, while an outer process adjusts hyperparameters. Gradient-based methods differentiate through these levels using unrolled optimization or the implicit function theorem. Previous work bounded their uniform stability from above, but it was unclear how closely those bounds captured possible instability.

This paper develops lower bounds, showing how unstable these methods can be in constructed cases. The difficulty is that each outer update depends on the current stage of inner optimization. The authors introduce expansion properties that quantify growth in differences, connecting outer-level hyperparameter divergence with the sensitivity of the inner optimization output.

Using those tools, they construct a quadratic example that yields tight lower bounds for the unrolling-based algorithm and meaningful bounds for a representative implicit-function-based algorithm. Tightness means that the corresponding uniform-stability analysis for the unrolling method has reached its limit. The result concerns the power of that analytical measure; it does not establish that every practical run has poor generalization.
neurips-2024-lower-bounds-of-uniform-sta.tldr: Constructed lower bounds show that uniform-stability analysis is tight for an unrolling-based hyperparameter optimizer.

paragraphs: Vision-language tracking follows an object using both visual information and a language description. A fixed initial prompt can become less useful as the target changes during a video. MemVLT addresses this by incorporating memory so that the guidance supplied to the tracker can adapt to those changes over time.

The design takes inspiration from Complementary Learning Systems theory. It includes modules for storing memories and allowing short-term and long-term memories to interact. Those interactions generate adaptive prompts, replacing dependence on the initial multimodal description alone. The practical role of memory is to keep tracking guidance responsive to the target's evolving appearance.

Experiments on MGIT, TNL2K, LaSOT, and LaSOT_ext report new state-of-the-art performance. MemVLT reaches 69.4% AUC on MGIT and 63.3% on TNL2K, with reported improvements of 8.4% and 4.7% over the prior best results. These findings support adaptive memory as a useful component for vision-language tracking, particularly when static guidance is insufficient for dynamically changing targets.
neurips-2024-memvlt-vision-language-trac.tldr: MemVLT uses interacting short-term and long-term memories to adapt tracking prompts as a target changes.

paragraphs: Counterfactual reasoning asks what would happen under a different scenario and can support explanations and decisions. This paper argues that scenarios generated by Pearl's approach can sometimes depart too far from observed data to be feasible. The authors illustrate that concern with simple examples and propose a framework for more natural counterfactuals.

Their method allows limited backtracking: when needed, it can change variables that causally precede the variable of interest. The aim is to keep the resulting scenario closer to realistic combinations of values in the actual data distribution. Backtracking is therefore a controlled part of constructing the alternative scenario, rather than an unrestricted revision of its history.

An optimization framework governs these changes through a naturalness criterion, permitting backtracking while controlling its extent. Empirical experiments demonstrate the method's effectiveness. The contribution is a way to connect causal counterfactual construction with distributional feasibility, so that an explanation can account for which preceding changes are needed to make an alternative scenario more realistic.
neurips-2024-natural-counterfactuals-wit.tldr: A naturalness-guided optimization framework permits controlled causal backtracking to generate more distributionally feasible counterfactuals.

paragraphs: FUNGI improves the representations produced by pretrained transformer encoders without training their weights further. It extracts additional information from how self-supervised objectives respond to each input. The idea is to use the resulting gradients as features alongside the model's ordinary output embedding, expanding what a downstream method can use.

For each input, the method computes gradients from several self-supervised objectives, projects them into fewer dimensions, and concatenates them with the embedding. The authors evaluate these combined features using nearest-neighbor classification on 11 vision datasets, five language datasets, and two audio datasets. Across different backbone sizes and pretraining strategies, the combined features consistently improve on embeddings alone.

The paper also reports benefits for linear classification, clustering, and image retrieval. In retrieval-based in-context scene understanding, FUNGI improves DINO's semantic-segmentation performance by a reported 17% without training. The findings show that a frozen model can supply useful information beyond its standard forward representation: input-specific gradients can enrich the features available for several downstream uses.
neurips-2024-no-train-all-gain-self-supe.tldr: FUNGI augments frozen model embeddings with compressed self-supervised gradients, improving representations without additional training.

paragraphs: Repeated self-attention can cause representations to collapse toward a rank-one subspace, reducing their ability to express distinct information. This paper asks how attention masks and layer normalization change that behavior. Its analysis expands beyond pure attention to examine components that could alter the consequences of increasing depth.

For masked attention without LayerNorm, the authors still find exponential rank collapse. However, sparse or local masks can provably slow the collapse rate. With LayerNorm, the result depends on the value matrices: certain classes still produce exponential convergence to rank one, so normalization alone does not universally prevent collapse.

The authors also construct counterexamples showing that suitable value matrices can prevent a general class of sequences from converging to rank one. Moreover, the same LayerNorm attention dynamics can have equilibria spanning every rank from one to full rank. These findings refute the hypothesis that LayerNorm has no role in rank collapse and establish a richer range of possible dynamics than pure-attention analyses suggest.
neurips-2024-on-the-role-of-attention-ma.tldr: Attention masks can slow rank collapse, while LayerNorm can support non-collapsing dynamics for suitable value matrices.

paragraphs: Open-vocabulary tracking aims to follow objects belonging to categories that were not seen during training. It extends the challenge of recognizing unfamiliar categories in individual images to tracking multiple objects through video. This paper identifies a shortage of benchmarks as one reason that video tracking has received less attention than open-vocabulary image detection.

The authors introduce OVT-B, containing 1,048 object categories, 1,973 videos, and 637,608 bounding-box annotations. It is substantially larger than the comparison dataset described in the abstract, OVTAO-val, which has more than 200 categories and more than 900 videos. The expanded coverage provides a larger basis for evaluating this tracking setting.

The paper also introduces a baseline that incorporates motion features, an important tracking signal overlooked by earlier open-vocabulary tracking methods. Experiments support both the benchmark's usefulness and the method's effectiveness. Together, the public dataset and baseline contribute a place to measure progress and evidence that motion information remains valuable when the tracker must handle previously unseen object categories.
neurips-2024-ovt-b-a-new-large-scale-ben.tldr: OVT-B expands evaluation of open-vocabulary video tracking and introduces a baseline that incorporates object motion.

paragraphs: Zeroth-order optimization searches for better solutions using function evaluations rather than directly available gradients. Estimating a useful descent direction can require many queries. Linear interpolation can provide accurate estimates, but its sampling cost is often high. ReLIZO aims to reduce that cost by reusing function queries from earlier iterations.

The authors formulate gradient estimation as a linear optimization problem with a quadratic constraint and derive an analytical solution. Their formulation separates the required sample count from the number of optimization variables without requiring extra conditions. This makes previous queries usable while keeping the sample size unchanged, reducing the need for fresh evaluations at every iteration.

The method also allows some intermediate quantities used in gradient estimation to be retrieved directly by indexing, lowering computational complexity. Experiments cover simulation functions, black-box adversarial attacks, neural architecture search, and parameter-efficient language-model fine-tuning. They report effectiveness and efficiency across these settings. The contribution is therefore both query reuse and cheaper computation for extracting an update direction from the available observations.
neurips-2024-relizo-sample-reusable-line.tldr: ReLIZO reduces zeroth-order gradient-estimation costs by reusing earlier function queries through an analytically solved interpolation formulation.

paragraphs: This paper asks whether ordinary training can favor relationships that remain stable across environments without explicit invariance regularization. It studies a low-rank matrix-sensing problem in which every environment contains a shared, lower-rank signal plus a spurious component that varies substantially between environments. That structure is central to the theoretical result.

The proposed training setup applies large-batch stochastic gradient descent with a large step size sequentially within each environment. Differences between environments create oscillations that can provably prevent the model from learning their spurious signals. After a certain number of iterations, the model reaches the invariant solution in the analyzed setting.

By contrast, pooling all the data for SGD leads the model to learn both invariant and spurious components. The comparison shows that heterogeneity can help or fail to help depending on how training encounters it. The authors call the beneficial behavior implicit invariance learning: the interaction of the data structure and optimization procedure favors the shared signal without adding an explicit penalty for environment-specific information.
neurips-2024-the-implicit-bias-of-hetero.tldr: In a structured matrix-sensing setting, sequential large-step SGD can use environmental variation to avoid spurious signals and recover an invariant solution.

paragraphs: Touchstone addresses whether medical image benchmarks provide convincing evidence of performance beyond their own test sets. Small or closely matched test sets, simplified metrics, and unfair comparisons can make strong benchmark results an unreliable guide to real-world success. The authors introduce a large collaborative benchmark for segmenting nine types of abdominal organs.

The benchmark uses 5,195 training CT scans from 76 hospitals and 5,903 testing scans from 11 additional hospitals. This separation and diversity support evaluation under multiple distribution shifts and strengthen the statistical significance of comparisons. The evaluation therefore examines performance across varied testing conditions rather than relying only on data similar to the training set.

The authors invited 14 inventors to train 19 algorithms, while an independent team evaluated them on three test sets. They also assessed existing frameworks, including MONAI and nnU-Net, distinguishing these adaptable systems from individual algorithms. The contribution is an evaluation resource and process designed to improve the credibility of medical-segmentation comparisons, with continued expansion intended to support further algorithm development.
neurips-2024-touchstone-benchmark-are-we.tldr: Touchstone evaluates abdominal-organ segmentation through large, diverse hospital datasets and independent testing of inventor-trained algorithms.

paragraphs: Numerical PDE solvers use meshes to represent a spatial domain. Moving mesh points can improve accuracy without increasing the total number of degrees of freedom. Conventional sophisticated movement methods can be expensive and struggle with complex boundaries, while existing learned methods often require retraining for different equations or geometries and can produce inverted elements.

UM2N is designed to transfer mesh movement across settings after a single training process. It combines a Graph Transformer encoder that extracts features with a Graph Attention Network decoder that moves the mesh. The trained network can be applied without retraining to different mesh structures and size distributions, PDE types, and boundary geometries.

The authors evaluate it on advection, Navier-Stokes examples, and a real-world tsunami simulation. It outperforms existing learned mesh-movement methods on the reported benchmarks. Compared with a conventional Monge-Ampère PDE-based approach, it substantially accelerates mesh movement and works in scenarios where that method fails. These results support transferable mesh adaptation as a way to improve solver workflows across varied problems.
neurips-2024-towards-universal-mesh-move.tldr: UM2N learns mesh movement that transfers without retraining across varied meshes, PDEs, and geometries, with strong reported efficiency and performance.
